transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-19
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Omar Ruiz (Redwood CSM), Lena Ortiz (Sierra Tech HoMLOps), Marcus Hale (CTO), Priya Desai (PM), Evan Cho (Security)
Notes: Kickoff / onboarding for Redwood implementation (hosted -> dedicated pilot).

00:00 - Alex Kim: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. Welcome, this is Alex from Redwood. We're excited to get Sierra Tech onboarded.
00:12 - Lena Ortiz: Hi Alex, hi team. Thanks for setting this up. We're excited too. We've been evaluating a couple of options and want a smooth POC to validate latency and cost.
00:25 - Alex Kim: Awesome. Quick intros — Priya Shah our SE will drive the technical plan, Omar is your CSM for the rollout. Could you go over high level goals, Lena?
00:35 - Lena Ortiz: Sure. Our goals: (1) move inference for two core models to Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput, (2) keep PII in our VPC for compliance, (3) validate latency under 100ms p95 for the customer-facing API, and (4) get lifecycle tooling for canary rollouts. We also need SOC 2 logs and KMS integration for keys.
00:55 - Marcus Hale: And timeline — legal wants a pilot by end of August, production by end of Q4, so aggressive.
01:05 - Alex Kim: Great. That aligns with the usual onboarding cadence. We'll plan a two-phase pilot: initial benchmarking + integration, then a capacity/resiliency run. Priya, I'll hand to you for technical scope.
01:18 - Priya Shah: Thanks. A few clarifying q's: which model architectures are we moving first? Are these Transformer decoders, two-stage reranker, embeddings? Also what are your typical sequence lengths?
01:30 - Lena Ortiz: Primary models are a 7B chat-style decoder used for summaries and a 2B reranker for search relevance. Average sequence length is 128 tokens but we have spikes to 512 for long docs. QPS currently about 50 steady, peaks ~220.
01:48 - Priya Shah: Good, that helps. For the Dedicated pilot we'll size GPU pools with headroom for bursts — our autoscaling + burst policy can cover the 220 peaks. We'll also recommend a quantization profile for the 7B to lower unit cost; Redwood Optimize will suggest it after initial traces.
02:05 - Evan Cho: Quick security note: we need KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, SAML SSO for RBAC. Also data retention policies must be configurable — we cannot retain raw customer inputs beyond 30 days.
02:17 - Omar Ruiz: We have SOC 2 + support for KMS and SAML. We will send the security pack and the audit log schematic. There may be a short checklist for on‑prem network requirements if you go private VPC.
02:29 - Marcus Hale: Is there any difference in latency profiles between Hosted and Dedicated? We worry about jitter.
02:36 - Priya Shah: Dedicated typically gives more predictable p95 via reserved GPU pools; jitter is lower because of capacity isolation. That said, batching and KV cache behavior can make p50 look higher sometimes if batches fill. We can tune batching thresholds to keep p95 <100ms as you requested.
02:53 - Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. I'm also concerned about fallbacks — what happens if capacity is constrained?
03:00 - Alex Kim: We support smart routing and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant (lower precision or alternative model). We'll document the policy in the rollout plan.
03:10 - Priya Shah: Also we'll set up prefix/KV cache to reduce repeated costs for session-based chats. Just a note: cache hits are very dependent on your prompt patterns. We'll instrument that in the benchmark.
03:22 - Marcus Hale: Ok. For the pilot, what benchmarks will you run? Latency, throughput, cost, and correctness?
03:28 - Priya Shah: Correct. We'll run (1) latency p50/p95, (2) throughput under steady and burst QPS, (3) token cost estimates with and without quantization, and (4) qualitative correctness checks for summaries — we'll use a small eval set you provide. We'll share a benchmark spreadsheet link later.
03:45 - Lena Ortiz: On the eval set: we'll scrub PII first, but we can provide 200 sample prompts and expected outputs.
03:52 - Priya Shah: Perfect. That will let us run Rouge/embedding-based similarity checks.
04:00 - Evan Cho: Regarding networking: we will likely prefer VPC peering for the pilot. What is the private control plane footprint?
04:07 - Omar Ruiz: For VPC the control plane is customer-managed but we have a private option where data plane sits in your VPC. We'll include the network diagram and required firewall rules in the security pack.
04:18 - Alex Kim: To keep things practical, here are immediate deliverables: Redwood sends onboarding deck, SOW and security pack; customer shares models, evals, and QPS metrics; then we schedule capacity sizing.
04:34 - Marcus Hale: For legal and procurement, do you have a standard SLA for Dedicated?
04:39 - Alex Kim: Yes — we have SLA tiers. For Dedicated pilot we'll propose a time-limited credit program and a standard enterprise SLA for production. I'll include pricing tiers in the SOW.
04:50 - Evan Cho: Any third-party dependencies? We use HashiCorp Vault for secrets and AWS KMS for keys — will Redwood integrate?
04:56 - Priya Shah: We integrate with customer KMS; we can support Vault via our connector. We'll capture exact flows in the security pack.
05:05 - Lena Ortiz: Ok. Who owns what for the first week?
05:09 - Omar Ruiz: I'll coordinate onboarding tasks. Action items: Alex to send deck & SOW; Lena to send model list & metrics; Priya to draft benchmark plan. We'll aim to have the benchmark run in two weeks.
05:22 - Alex Kim: Quick question — have you evaluated Anthropic or OpenAI for this workload? Any gotchas?
05:27 - Marcus Hale: We ran a short eval with ManagedCloudAI, cost was higher and latency more variable. We're looking for predictability and on‑prem control.
05:35 - Priya Shah: Understood. That will inform our routing and model selection. We'll also propose a quantized 7B and a float 7B fallback if you need quality parity.
05:46 - Lena Ortiz: About data retention again, can you confirm we can configure logs to expire and that raw request data can be disabled?
05:52 - Omar Ruiz: Yes, we support configurable retention and can redact raw request payloads. We'll include retention settings in the onboarding checklist.
06:00 - Alex Kim: Let's capture explicit next steps and dates so legal and PMs can track.
06:05 - Priya Desai: From product side we need clear success criteria: (1) pilot p95 < 100ms, (2) cost per 1k tokens within X% of target — we'll define X in the SOW, (3) SAML + KMS integration validated.
06:20 - Alex Kim: We'll add those to the SOW.
06:24 - Priya Shah: A technical note: for the 512-token spikes we'll provision longer KV cache windows and tune attention kernel selection; sometimes sequence-length variance changes kernel choices which affects perf, we'll document observed profiles.
06:40 - Marcus Hale: If the quantized model causes small regressions in quality, what's the rollback path?
06:46 - Priya Shah: Rollbacks are simple: keep the float variant in the model catalog and set a canary rollout with automatic quality thresholds — Redwood Console can auto-rollback based on eval metrics you define.
06:57 - Lena Ortiz: Great. That helps our PMs be comfortable.
07:03 - Alex Kim: Any regulatory constraints about data residency?
07:06 - Evan Cho: We're US-only for now but may expand to EU later. We'll want region pinning.
07:11 - Omar Ruiz: We support region pinning in deployments; we'll note it as a future requirement.
07:17 - Priya Shah: Ok, timeline recap: Redwood sends materials by 7/21, Sierra sends data and evals by 7/23, week of 7/27 we'll have the sizing session, first benchmark run planned for week of 8/3, and pilot report by mid-August to enable legal review. Does that sequence work?
07:36 - Marcus Hale: Yes, that aligns.
07:39 - Lena Ortiz: Fine with me.
07:41 - Alex Kim: Perfect. Any other open questions?
07:45 - Evan Cho: Nothing immediate. We'll review the security pack.
07:48 - Priya Desai: Please include the benchmark spreadsheet as a shared Google sheet.
07:52 - Priya Shah: Will do. I'll own the sheet and invite your team.
07:55 - Alex Kim: Ok, wrapping up — recap of action items and owners. Omar will follow up with calendar invites for sizing, Priya will share benchmark plan and sheet, Alex will send SOW/security deck.
08:10 - Lena Ortiz: Thanks all, appreciate it. Looking forward to the pilot.
08:14 - Alex Kim: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with links (onboarding deck, security pack, benchmark spreadsheet).

Shared artifacts referenced:
- Onboarding deck: link sent via email (placeholder)
- Security pack: redwood.com/security-pack (placeholder link)
- Benchmark spreadsheet: link to Google sheet (to be shared by Priya)

End of transcript.
